searches.note: Twenty six searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's, two left unspent. The five shared searches went to the three DOs (the Getaria order of 1989 and its widening of 2007, the Bizkaia order of 1994, the Álava order of 2001), read through the BOE, the BOPV, the Basque government and the Diputación Foral de Gipuzkoa as primary, and to the Basque grape names. The houses' own domains were searched twice by restriction (txominetxaniz.com for its sheets and its training, txakoliameztoi.com for Rubentis and the parral), each read as primary through its summary. The rest went to the open web with the author's sources blocked (the houses' domains, Cellar Tours, Decanter, De Maison, Flatiron, Spanish Wine Lover, Deia, Alliance Wine) so that an independent account could be heard. No fetch tried. Two writers' own sites met in the results are cited nowhere.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the DO and its order, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the governing texts for the three DOs, then to independent accounts of each house's dates and people, then to merchants' and importers' sheets of each wine for the blend, the months and the vessels, the author's sources blocked.

Where the sheets disagreed and none was primary, the figure was hedged as each source's or cut; where a fact rested on one account and was found nowhere by the refuter (the brothers of 1980, the training on wires, the experiment after claret, the plots by place, Apardune's 22 to 36 months), it was taken out or put as the sources have it.

tested: The vines of 1649, with the house, Cellar Tours and Decanter blocked: Qcom.es, Jorge Ordóñez Selections and The Spanish Acquisition give 1649 and Domingo de Etxaniz (Txomin is the Basque Domingo) in the protocol archives of Gipuzkoa. Borne out as the family's account; every page repeats the house's text and none gives the archive's reference, so the story's 'traces' stays and the archive itself stays open.

The revival of 1980 and the DO: The Spanish Acquisition and an importer's page tell the revival from 1980 led by one member of the Txueka family, among the founders of the DO in 1989; no source read names brothers. The DO's order of 21 September 1989 (BOPV of 25 October 1989) is borne out by the BOE's own resolution of 2009 and the Basque government's page, the first zone Aia, Getaria and Zarautz by both, and the widening to all Gipuzkoa in 2007 by the Diputación Foral de Gipuzkoa and Wikipedia. Bizkaia's 1994 and Álava's 2001 are borne out by the BOE and the BOPV, so the first of the three DOs stands.

The grapes of the white: merchants give nine tenths Hondarrabi Zuri (Jorge Ordóñez, El Pilar), 85 and 15 (González Byass's sheet of the 2020), 95 and 5 (an old sheet), and half of each for the 2025 (Decantalo, Bodeboca); the house's sheet names Hondarrabi Zuri alone. The great majority in most accounts overstated the agreement: changed.

The training: Jorge Ordóñez and El Pilar give a pergola with wires on the steeper slopes, Decantalo and Ardoa give wires; the house's own pages, searched on its domain, say nothing of training. Trained on wires could not be settled and is cut from the sites and the story.

The other wines on the house's own sheets: Eugenia a sparkling white of Hondarrabi Zuri made by the traditional method, Uydi a late harvest Hondarrabi Zuri from old vines picked in November and kept on its lees, the Rosado a sheet of its own. Borne out; the notes now say what the sheets say.

The house rules: nobody living named (the leader of the revival is described, the Txueka Etxaniz line named as a family as the house names it), no price, no score, nothing volatile (the hectares met in two results are not used), British, no dash. The serve of 8 to 10 degrees with the house's colder advice beside it stands; the making on the house's sheet stands.

The share of Beltza: two merchants give half of each for the 2025 vintage, against a tenth or less elsewhere; it may be a slip copied between shops.
The state's ratification of the DO by an order of 6 April 1990 was met in one result and is not used.

tested: The family's dates, with the house, De Maison, Flatiron and Spanish Wine Lover blocked: Txakoli.eu, Go Local San Sebastian and several merchants give 1820; the generations are five by some and seven by others. The story's 1820 by the family's own account and five generations as it tells them stand, with 1860 left as the importer's.

Rubentis's making: Serendipity Wines and Durham Wine give the grapes destemmed together, pressed directly and fermented with native yeasts in steel at 15 degrees Celsius for some twenty days, the tanks closed towards the end to keep the gas, never force carbonated; a critic's note gives the same with ambient yeasts. Borne out. One page speaks of the house's own selection of yeasts: noted, not used.
The parral: a merchant (Wine Solutions) gives the traditional elevated parral for the house's vines, with the author's two; borne out.

The story's experiment after the pale claret style wines of the past: the house's own Rubentis page, searched on its domain, says the colour recalls the ancestral txakoli of the Cantabrian coast and nowhere calls it an experiment. Changed to what the house says.

Hijo de Rubentis: traditional method, Hondarrabi Beltza and Zuri with a fifth fermented in oak casks, an average of three years in the cellar by the house; merchants give 14 months on the lees for 2015 and 2016 and at least 36 months for another. The three years is now hedged as the house's average.

The house rules: the generation head named in two results is living and not named; no price, no score, no hectares (40, 20 and 51 met and not used), British, no dash. The label's still means not sparkling, which the lint's note on the present does not touch.

livingNote: None of these is named in the fragment's prose; the read together agent adds those it judges living to people.json. Described, never named, for want of dates in two sources: Domingo de Etxaniz, the forebear of 1649 (long dead, but no dates), the founders of Itsasmendi and of Señorío de Astobiza. swapNote: The author proposed no swap, and the refuter proposes none. Txomin Etxaniz, Ameztoi, Itsasmendi, Doniene Gorrondona and Señorío de Astobiza are each a house of its DO known by name abroad, two of Getaria, two of Bizkaia and the reference house of Álava, and each pick's wine is the one the house is known by: the Txomin Etxaniz white, Rubentis, Itsasmendi 7, the Gorrondona white and the Astobiza white.
planNotes: txomin-etxaniz: answered. The family's part in the DO of 1989 rests on the house and on two pages that name the leader of the revival among the DO's founders; the records of the seventeenth century are the protocol archives of 1649, the family's account repeated everywhere and never with a reference; the label words are Getariako Txakolina and the house's name.

ameztoi: answered. Rubentis is Getariako Txakolina, a rosé of Hondarrabi Beltza and Zuri fermented together; the about half of each is the author's two pages and was not contradicted; 1820 by the family's account and several pages, 1860 by its importer, so founded stays empty; the white is the other wine.

itsasmendi: answered in part, and the why needs a change. The why's Gernika house of 1995 runs two facts together: 1995 is the first winery, at Muskiz, and the house dates its own founding to 1994; the move to Gernika is 2001, 2002 or 2003. The grapes of 7 are Hondarrabi Zuri, Zerratia and Riesling in every account; why it is called 7 was found nowhere.

doniene-gorrondona: answered.
